precepts.text: The angel tells Ezra his mind is gone too far in the world, so his thoughts are not our thoughts.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure because the prophecies in this Bible are sure; we have a more sure word of prophecy. Did we not go into slavery on ships like the Most High declared through Moses in Deuteronomy 28? We are living proof that the Bible is real.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
The angel tells Ezra, “Thy heart hath gone to far in this world, and thinkest thou to comprehend the way of the most High?” Ezra's mind had gone too far in the world, and he could not comprehend the way of the Most High on his own.

His thoughts are not our thoughts. That is why it takes conversion; a mind gone far into this world cannot just decide to follow the Bible. The law of the Lord is what converts the soul.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Now the question might be, why doesn’t the Lord judge everybody at the same time when he returns? Why does he wait for a thousand years and then cast people into the lake of fire? How many people are on earth in 2023: about 8 billion, and that’s a rough estimate that Esau came up with. Why doesn’t he do it all at once? That’s the same thing Ezra asked.

“Go thy way to a woman with child, and ask of her when she hath fulfilled her nine months, if her womb may keep the birth any longer within her. Then said I, No, Lord, that can she not. And he said unto me, In the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman.” Stop, look at that: in the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman. Meaning what? Those souls that were in the grave come back, just like the woman gives birth: the dead, they come back. But guess what: the group that goes into the lake of fire, they don’t come back. They stay right there.

“For like as a woman that travaileth maketh haste to escape the necessity of the travail: even so do these places haste to deliver those things that are committed unto them.” They haste to give those spirits back up, to have them come back. That’s the sea and death and hell giving up the dead which were in them.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 6 The 4 Horsemen

precepts.why: The souls of the prophets speak to the Lord. No, your mama doesn't speak to the Lord; the Lord doesn't want to hear nothing your mama has to say. These are the ones that were murdered and killed, or died following the Bible. Your mama followed Cesare Borgia; God doesn't want to hear nothing she has to say. “Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers,” See that: the souls of the righteous speak to God. All people that die in sin, God ain't listening to them; they ain't saying nothing. So don't make excuses for your grandma: she always read the Bible, but she was worshipping the devil, so God ain't listening to her. “saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when cometh the fruit of the floor of our reward?” See that: the righteous always talk before the Lord. So when you die in this truth, all praises, you are going to talk to the Lord.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
“Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord”. Prophetically, nowadays, this is the so-called white man: a group of people who have counsel they think the Lord don’t see. “And their works are in the dark”: all the evil that they do is in the dark. Today they call this think tanks: men and women, the smartest of the nations, the ones that go to places like Yale, Harvard and Oxford, the crème de la crème, the cream of the crop, and they pay them millions of dollars each.

There was a robbery in Manhattan and the Bishop’s unit was called. A white man got beat up and robbed, and in his room were books all over the whole huge apartment, on the floor, on the walls, everywhere. They could all smell the weed; that’s why he was robbed. Asked what he does for a living, he said he works for a think tank, a very popular think tank: he gets paid to read. He only goes out of his house maybe once a week for groceries. They call him, give him a subject and say, we want you to give us an insight on this. Then at the end of the month or two months they all get together on how to confound: rap music, drugs, feminism. This is how you do it. They read all the history books and search out things you would not believe. They got books we ain’t got, books Negroes ain’t never seen.

“And they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?” Who would believe it’s us? They think they can never be figured out.

“Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter’s clay”. They have turned God’s words upside down. That’s what the archangel Uriel was telling Ezra: if this grain of evil seed be not turned upside down, it won’t come; it must be turned upside down. Isaiah is prophesying to us. They turn God’s laws, this whole world, upside down: righteousness is evil and evil is righteousness.

The potter’s clay: on the potter’s wheel it spins real fast, and with the clay you can make anything, a cup or a tray, whatever. And whatever you make, you can undo too: if you don’t like it you can just push it down, because the clay is real soft, malleable.

“For shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not?” We’re the work; God made us. “Or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?” That’s what the white man says: there is no God, he didn’t make me.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: “And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also”. They said the disciples have turned the world upside down, meaning they turned it right side up. The prophets’ job, the disciples’ job: all that evil that we see, turn it upside down, meaning right side up.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
That’s our job: we see the evil, we gotta turn the evil upside down, making it right side up. “For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal”: we’re not using guns and knives and sticks or bats, “but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Brothers and sisters, our job is to pull down strongholds. Christianity is a stronghold; we must pull it down. Islam is a stronghold; we must pull it down. Egyptology is a stronghold; we must pull it down. Feminism is a stronghold; we must pull it down. The LGBT community is a stronghold; we must pull it down. Just to name a few.

“Casting down imaginations”: we must cast down all evil imaginations. You might imagine Jesus Christ is white; our job is to cast that thought down. You might imagine Christ was born December 25th; our job is to cast that down, using the Bible of course. You might imagine the woman is the head of society; we have to cast that imagination down.

“And every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”: our job is to cast down every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, meaning against the Bible. “And bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”: we got to bring every man and every woman’s thought to what this Bible says, so they acknowledge, yes, the word of God is true.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
“Behold, the Lord maketh the earth empty”: he’s going to wipe these nations out. “And maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down”: meaning he’s going to turn everything right side up. The wicked already turned it upside down, so when God turns it upside down it’s gonna be right side up.

But it starts with us. The Lord ain’t gonna do nothing until we put the boots on the ground. You men, fulfill your role in the street; you women, teach them children, teach them young sisters. Cast down all evil imaginations; turn every lie upside down. Then God’s gonna step in. And when the Lord steps in, he “scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof”: he’s gonna scatter the nations, and destruction.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
Paul told you the same thing. If you had the question why did Adam listen to Eve: the Most High made it that way. “For the creature was made subject to vanity”: the creature means man, beginning with Adam, and vanity means sin. Adam was made subject to sin.

“Not willingly”: not saying, Lord, I want to sin; that’s not what Adam’s mindset was. “But by reason of him”: by reason of God, “who hath subjected the same in hope”. His plan was to subject man in hope, hoping in his son Christ. That’s what God’s plan was from the beginning.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The same grain of evil seed sown in the heart of Adam: he bore a wicked heart, and so do all born of him.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
The same thing being said in the New Testament. “For Adam was first formed, then Eve”: Adam was formed first, then came the woman. “And Adam was not deceived”: he was not tricked. “But the woman being deceived was in the transgression”: the woman was the one deceived by the serpent; Adam was not.

So once again, why did Adam sin, why did he follow her? Because God put that wicked heart in him, and he said, you know what, I’m going to listen to her. That’s what we call today presumptuous sin: I know it’s wrong but I’m gonna do it anyway. That was God’s plan from the beginning, and that’s what Paul was making reference to. Adam was not tricked, so stop saying that; he knew exactly what he was doing.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
Ezra is complaining: “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” You ain’t fallen alone, Adam. That’s why David said, in sin did my mother conceive me: all of us are born with that sin nature in us.

“For what profit is it unto us, if there be promised us an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?” We’re sinning, we’re breaking God’s laws. “Whereas ourselves being most wicked are made vain”. “And that there are laid up for us dwellings of health and safety, whereas we have lived wickedly?” We’re not going to attain to that; we’re not going to get it. “Whereas we have walked in the most wicked ways of all”: that’s all of us in here, all of us listening.

“And that there should be shewed a paradise, whose fruit endureth for ever, wherein is security and medicine”: that paradise is New Jerusalem on earth, “since we shall not enter into it? (For we have walked in unpleasant places.)” The unpleasant places is sin.

“And that the faces of them which have used abstinence shall shine above the stars”: abstinence means when you refrain yourself from breaking God’s laws. Those men and women have abstained from worshipping other gods, from dishonouring their parents, from killing, from stealing, from committing adultery, from bearing false witness against their neighbour. “Whereas our faces shall be blacker than darkness?”

“For while we lived and committed iniquity”: we broke God’s commandments, “we considered not that we should begin to suffer for it after death.” Don’t let a Black Hebrew Israelite fool you and say you can sin all you want and when you die you’re going to become a baby in the kingdom. That’s a lie. You’re going to live the life of Riley, commit adultery, steal, lie, and still get the kingdom of heaven in Jesus’ name, amen? It says you’re gonna suffer after you die. That’s some heavy stuff; that should put some fear in you.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.” Watch this: “For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” Christ is going to kill a whole lot of people. A whole lot.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
When the ears of corn shall be cut down, which are without number: “And the slain of the Lord shall be at that day from one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth”. God is going to kill millions upon millions of people. That’s why I don’t see why people play with the Bible: I’m just going to be wicked and the Lord gonna forgive me. That ain’t what the Bible says.

“They shall not be lamented”: ain’t nobody gonna cry for your dead body. “Neither gathered, nor buried; they shall be dung upon the ground.” That’s what the Bible says. I ain’t making it up.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: “The most High hath made this world for many, but the world to come for few.” God made this world for many, but the New Jerusalem for few. He compares it like dust: “There be many created, but few shall be saved.” There’s many created in this world, but few shall be saved. Christians can’t understand.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: Watch this, about the other nations: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”. The multitude of nations, God said let them perish, because they were born in vain. “And let my grape be kept, and my plant”: the nation of Israel. “For with great labour have I made it perfect.”

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
John tells the same thing Ezra was told about the dead in their chambers. “And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held”. And they cry “with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true”, dost thou “not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?” It is the same question: how long.

That shows you that when you die, brothers, you don’t die; when you die, sisters, you don’t die. Meaning the real you. We think the host we are in right now is the real us. It is not. This is the temporary thing; all these bodies go back to the dust. But the real man, the real woman, the real soul, the real spirit goes before the Lord, and you are living.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: Ezra’s question was when cometh the fruit of the floor of our reward. Isaiah answers it: “Behold, the Lord hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him”. Thy salvation comes, and his reward is with him. We want that reward.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
Remember what Ezra asked: when cometh the fruit of the floor of our reward, when will we get our reward for keeping the commandments. Christ speaks of the same reward: “Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven”. Rejoice about it. Don’t get mad.

“Great is your reward in heaven” means New Jerusalem on earth: thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

“For so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.” They persecuted the prophets before you the same way. That is the course we have to pay.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why:
Read the verse above it: “Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.” Brothers, if you ain’t got no haters you are doing something wrong; you ain’t pushing the right buttons. When you are keeping the commandments you will get haters, like the geriatric crew out there that hate us.

“Falsely” is the key: when they speak falsely against you for Christ’s sake. That is when the reward of verse 12 is yours.

note.label: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

precepts.why:
Let’s get an understanding of that perpetual seed that corrupted us when we got to this earth. “For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness hath it brought up unto this time?” Didn’t Adam have the kingdom? He had a kingdom, but he lost it through sin. Didn’t the nation of Israel have the kingdom? Israel had the same thing.

How much ungodliness has it brought up unto this time: our forefathers didn’t learn from Adam’s mistake; we kept that thing going. “And how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?” That time of threshing is the harvest. Evil is going to increase, a lot of evil; Isaiah said the earth is going to be turned into utter darkness. The evil is just going to keep going until the time of threshing comes.

note.label: | Explaining Dark Sentences | Part 3

precepts.why: This is some dark stuff right here. “Go thy way to a woman with child, and ask of her when she hath fulfilled her nine months, if her womb may keep the birth any longer within her.” So how long does a woman have to carry children now? Nine months. Hold that against 2 Esdras 6:21, where in the kingdom the women bring forth at three or four months.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “In the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman”: what does the womb of a woman bring forth? Life. It is telling you from the grave the soul goes back through the woman again. We will go over that in more detail in another class.

precepts.why: Listen to what the angel said. “And the angel that was sent unto me, whose name was Uriel, gave me an answer”.

points: “I beseech thee, O Lord, let me have understanding”. Ezra already had understanding, but he wanted a higher level of understanding.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “For it was not my mind to be curious of the high things”. The angel Uriel was getting on him, so Ezra had to come back and say it’s not his mind to be curious of high things. Some of us be curious of high things, asking what the kingdom is gonna look like. How are we gonna know? All we can give is a biblical description. How tall Christ is going to be? That’s too high; we gotta wait and see.

“But of such as pass by us daily”: regular things on earth. “Wherefore Israel is given up as a reproach to the heathen, and for what cause the people whom thou hast loved is given over unto ungodly nations”: why are we given over unto ungodly nations? At this time we were under Persia-Media, not the Greeks. “And why the law of our forefathers is brought to nought, and the written covenants come to none effect”.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “And we pass away out of the world as grasshoppers, and our life is astonishment and fear, and we are not worthy to obtain mercy.” Ezra acknowledges how wicked we as a people are: we are not worthy to receive mercy.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “What will he then do unto his name whereby we are called?” Lord, what are you going to do with the name of Israel? “Of these things have I asked”: that’s what Ezra wants to know.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: Ezra is talking to the archangel Uriel. “The more thou searchest, the more thou shalt marvel”: the more you try to search that out, the more you’re going to be shocked. “For the world hasteth fast to pass away”: the world is going by fast.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “And cannot comprehend the things that are promised to the righteous in time to come”. That’s why the Lord said ‘eyes have not seen’ what the Lord has prepared for those that love him. It’s beyond our understanding, our comprehension. “For this world is full of unrighteousness and infirmities.”

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “For the evil is sown, but the destruction thereof is not yet come.” Evil is sown into the earth, but the end, the destruction, has not come yet.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “If therefore that which is sown be not turned upside down”: there’s a lot in there, and the class peeled back the onion on this verse. Evil is sown in the earth, and the angel tells Ezra that if that evil is not turned upside down, it won’t come. The grain of evil seed must be turned upside down. So our job, brothers and sisters, is to turn the evil upside down, and then the Lord will step in.

“And if the place where the evil is sown pass not away”: meaning made empty, destroyed, like Isaiah 24:1. “Then cannot it come that is sown with good”: then the kingdom cannot come. If that does not happen, the kingdom cannot come.
Don’t think we’re not going to pay a price for this. Did not Christ pay a price? Did not Paul, James and John pay a price? Even Mary and Martha; all the women of God paid the price.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning”: when God created Adam he put an evil heart in him. Why would God do that? The Most High made it that way; that was his plan from the beginning.

“And how much ungodliness hath it brought up unto this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?” It’s going to get worse and worse until the time of threshing come. What is the time of threshing? Jeremiah 51:33: the threshing of the daughter of Babylon.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “Ponder now by thyself, how great fruit of wickedness the grain of evil seed hath brought forth.” The angel tells Ezra: I want you to ponder on this, think about this, meditate on this, from the time of Adam until the time of threshing, how great the fruit of wickedness is that the grain of evil seed hath brought forth. Now the question might be, how much fruit of wickedness has come forth? Let’s just take a look: First Timothy 1:9.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: Back to the title verses: “For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning”. “Ponder now by thyself, how great fruit of wickedness the grain of evil seed hath brought forth.” I gave you an example of how great a wicked seed this world has brought forth. I just gave you a few examples, but there’s a lot more.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “And when the ears shall be cut down”. It’s like when you go through a cornfield and you cut down the ears of corn. The ears represent the people, “which are without number”. “How great a floor shall they fill?”
When Christ comes, it’s going to kill a lot of people. Christians will say no, you ain’t. Here’s the proof.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: Then Ezra asks: “How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?” He wants to know when the end of all this wickedness will come.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “Do not thou hasten above the most Highest: for thy haste is in vain to be above him”. You can’t go above the Lord. This is Uriel’s warning to Ezra: “thou hast much exceeded”, you have gone too far in what you are asking.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

points: “Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers”. When we die, we are in our chambers in heaven, and the righteous there ask the same question: “How long shall I hope on this fashion? when cometh the fruit of the floor of our reward?”

When will all this evil be over, and when shall we get a reward for keeping the commandments? That is the question. That is why, when we die, we ask the Lord when he is going to bring vengeance on them that dwell upon the earth, when he is going to bring judgment on America. When, Lord, when?
